html:
The Great Famine of 1876 to 1878 struck south and west India after the monsoon failed, killing somewhere between about five and ten million people. It was worst in the Madras Presidency, Mysore, Hyderabad and the Bombay Deccan.

The drought was part of a worldwide pattern tied to a strong El Niño; northern China suffered at the same time in the Northern Chinese Famine. But policy turned a crop failure into mass death. The viceroy, Lord Lytton, believed in free markets and in keeping relief spending low. Grain kept moving by rail to the ports and abroad. People on relief works got a ration so small that many starved while working.

In January 1877, at the height of the famine, Lytton held the Delhi Durbar to proclaim Queen Victoria Empress of India, a grand feast that critics never forgot.

Afterwards a Famine Commission wrote rules for future relief, the famine codes. Indian nationalists used the famine as proof that British rule drained the country. It was one in the long line that began with the Bengal famine of 1770.
sum: The Great Famine of 1876 to 1878 struck south and west India after the monsoon failed, killing somewhere between about five and ten million people. It was worst in the Madras Presidency, Mysore, Hyderabad and the Bombay Deccan.
